title: Systematic Review: Trends in Intelligent Tutoring Systems in Mathematics Teaching and Learning
venue: International Journal of Education in Mathematics, Science, and Technology (IJEMST)
extended_summary:
This paper examines the current state of intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) in mathematics teaching and learning, with a particular focus on higher education institutions and some attention to secondary education. The review asks what purposes ITSs serve, what advantages and limitations are reported, how effective they appear to be, whether user modeling and adaptive processes are included, and what research methodologies are being used in this literature.

The intervention studied is not a single program but the broader class of AI-enabled and adaptive intelligent tutoring systems used for mathematics education. Across 43 documents published between 2012 and 2022, the review catalogs systems such as ALEKS, PAT2Math, GeoGebraTUTOR, MATHia, ASSISTments, and others. The paper synthesizes how these systems are used for personalization, assessment, feedback, problem solving, skill development, and instructional support, and it also summarizes the adaptive techniques used, including expert systems, predictive models, Bayesian networks, machine learning, and neural networks.

The population represented in the reviewed literature is primarily students in secondary school and early higher education mathematics, especially those studying foundational topics such as algebra, arithmetic, geometry, calculus, fractions, and problem solving. The review is based on 43 studies selected from Web of Science and Scopus-indexed journals and conferences. Because it is a systematic review of prior studies rather than a direct implementation, setting and intervention duration vary across included studies and are not reducible to a single implementation context.

The main conclusions are that ITSs in mathematics education are most often used to support personalized and adaptive learning and are frequently associated with improved academic performance, improved learning, immediate feedback, and stronger assessment and monitoring processes. At the same time, the review highlights recurring limitations in the literature, including small samples, short study durations, poor reporting of adaptation and student models, and a lack of longitudinal and generalizable research. The authors conclude that ITSs show clear promise for mathematics education, but stronger and longer-term research is still needed.

identified_tools.name: ITS
identified_tools.description: Intelligent tutoring systems are AI-supported instructional systems that provide interactive guidance, adaptive sequencing, problem-solving support, feedback, and learner-tailored tutoring.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of intelligent tutoring systems in mathematics teaching and learning across secondary and higher education contexts, based on 43 documents published from 2012-2022.

findings.finding_summary: Improvement in academic performance was the most commonly reported effectiveness outcome, appearing in 16 reviewed studies; improved learning was reported in 8 studies. The review synthesizes these as commonly reported positive mathematics learning outcomes of ITS use, without a pooled effect size.
findings.measure: Reported mathematics academic performance and learning outcomes across reviewed ITS studies

findings.finding_summary: Improved problem solving was reported in 8 reviewed studies, and step-by-step procedural support was identified as an advantage in 5 studies. The review presents these as commonly reported benefits of ITS-supported mathematics instruction.
findings.measure: Mathematical problem solving and procedural support

findings.finding_summary: Increased motivation was reported in 5 reviewed studies, and positive student perception was reported in 4 studies, indicating favorable affective responses to ITS use in mathematics learning in part of the reviewed literature.
findings.measure: Student motivation and positive perception toward ITS use

findings.finding_summary: Personalized and adaptive learning was the most frequently reported purpose of ITS use (18 studies) and was also reported as an effectiveness outcome in 5 studies. This indicates that adaptation/personalization was a central design goal and a less frequently reported outcome theme in the reviewed literature.

Increased participation was reported in 2 reviewed studies, and participation promotion was identified as an advantage in 4 studies; collaborative work was noted in 1 study. These findings suggest limited review-reported evidence for engagement-related benefits.
findings.measure: Participation, engagement, and collaborative work during mathematics learning

findings.finding_summary: Immediate feedback was cited in 10 reviewed studies, and evaluation or monitoring support in 7 studies, indicating that feedback and formative monitoring were commonly reported functional benefits of ITSs.
findings.measure: Immediate feedback, formative assessment, and monitoring support

findings.finding_summary: The review identified recurring implementation limitations, including small samples (9 studies), limited time (4 studies), connectivity issues (4 studies), and technical problems (2 studies). These were reported as common constraints affecting implementation or evaluation.
findings.measure: Implementation limitations including sample size, time, connectivity, and technical problems

findings.finding_summary: Positive results related to ITS design or underlying system algorithms were reported in 5 reviewed studies. This refers to system-level performance or design effectiveness rather than a pooled student learning effect.
findings.measure: Effectiveness of ITS design and underlying algorithms

identified_tools.name: ALEKS
identified_tools.description: Adaptive online learning platform for mathematics that assesses student knowledge and delivers individualized practice and instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: ALEKS is the most frequently used named ITS in the review, reported in 18.6% of the reviewed studies. The review says ALEKS guides the learning process, shows an individualized learning sequence, presents differentiated problems through questions, encourages participation, supports students with diverse performance levels, and requires less teacher supervision and assistance. It is listed in Table 10 as addressing mathematics and problem solving, and specific studies cited include Craig et al. (2013), Huang et al. (2013), and Raju et al. (2018).

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that ALEKS guides individualized learning sequences and differentiated problem solving, helping students with diverse performance levels in mathematics.
The review reports that ALEKS requires less teacher supervision and assistance in students' established learning plans.
The review reports that ALEKS encourages student participation during mathematics learning activities.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review of 43 studies on intelligent tutoring systems in mathematics education, which places it at the highest evidence tier under the provided framework. However, the reviewed studies themselves vary in rigor, and the paper is more descriptive synthesis than quantitative meta-analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports generally positive findings such as improved learning and academic performance, but it does not provide a pooled effect size or a consistent quantitative estimate of impact. Therefore, overall impact is promising but unclear in magnitude.
